text: Map Teleport is a series of map teleportation mods for Project Zomboid developed by Huaxin Zhang, known across platforms as Introvert Arcade. The current releases are the Right-Click Rescue character edition and the Vehicle & Trailer edition. While using some cheat mods, the developer would right-click the place she wanted to reach on the world map but could not find the Teleport Here option for moving her character. She made the character edition to address this difficulty, then gradually added support for animals, vehicles and trailers. She released the mods through Steam Workshop and continues to maintain them.
Origins

The developer repeatedly encountered a specific difficulty: when she wanted to teleport her character to a location on the map, right-clicking that location did not bring up Teleport Here, so she could not travel in this way. The world-map context menu also serves navigation, markers and other functions. Adding a teleport option therefore required checking that these actions remained usable.

She tried switching mods, changing their load order, and modifying code and key bindings. After each change, she had to check whether teleportation worked; some changes also meant adjusting an established way of playing. She could inspect and modify code, but players unfamiliar with programming might not be able to solve the problem in the same way. Learning to edit code or repeatedly switching tools was a considerable inconvenience just to use a teleport function. She therefore made Right-Click Rescue as a directly installable mod, adding a separate character teleport option to the world-map context menu so that other players facing similar difficulties would have less troubleshooting to do.

Right-Click Rescue retains the familiar action of right-clicking a destination on the world map, while preserving the other map actions when adding its teleport option. If teleportation moves only the character, vehicles and trailers still have to be retrieved, and rope-led animals may become separated from the player. Vehicles and trailers left far away can be difficult to recover and may be damaged. She had also seen requests for vehicle teleportation in comments on other cheat mods and in forum discussions. This led her to consider how animals and vehicle convoys could travel with the character.

text: Release environment

Steam Workshop provides a channel for publishing, subscribing to and updating mods. Project Zomboid's Lua modding mechanisms and development tools allow individual creators to adjust game rules and interactions, then share their work with players through the Workshop. [Steamworks Workshop documentation](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/workshop), [official game description](https://store.steampowered.com/app/108600/Project_Zomboid/)

Players often install mods by several creators at once, and some of those mods use the same menu or game interface. After the game or a mod is updated, functions that previously worked together may need to be checked again. She was using several mods when she encountered the difficulty described above, so her troubleshooting included switching mods and changing their load order. This describes the circumstances and the steps she tried; the specific cause has not been confirmed.

An early test mod in the Map Teleport series was publicly released on the Workshop. The Right-Click Rescue character edition and Vehicle & Trailer edition were released subsequently. Once testing of those two editions was complete, the early test mod was taken down.

For a mod creator, publication is only the beginning. Installation and usage instructions need to keep pace with new versions, and issues arising from different combinations of mods need follow-up. Players can use the Workshop page to learn about the mod, read update notes and report problems in comments.

text: Existing approaches

The Workshop already offers teleport tools with different interfaces. For example, [B42] Teleportation Menu (simple) uses a panel to set and select destinations, while the update notes for Cheat Menu Phoenix also include world-map right-click teleportation. These tools offer different ways to teleport, but the developer still needed an approach that worked in her own setup and met her requirements for accompanying animals and vehicles. Map Teleport addresses two practical needs: adding a separate teleport option to the world-map context menu so that players have a usable way to move their character, and allowing vehicles, trailers and animals to travel with that character. [Teleportation Menu Workshop page](https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3498389154), [Cheat Menu Phoenix Workshop page](https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3453422228)
Among the tools she found and tried at the time, none met all these requirements. This assessment is limited to the tools and versions she had actually used.
These experiences led to the three design responses in Table 1.

text: A player may know exactly where they want to go, yet find no teleport option after right-clicking that location on the map, leaving them to troubleshoot or use another method. Even after the character arrives, they may still need to return for vehicles or search for animals. The three design responses address these inconveniences, reducing the time spent investigating menus, retrieving vehicles or finding animals so that players can continue with their own plans.

Convenience features also change the experience of playing. Teleportation reduces the risks of travel and changes how vehicles and supplies are transported; for some players, those activities are an important part of survival gameplay. The developer therefore makes a point of playing extensively and understanding the basic mechanics, values and parameters before reading community discussions and talking with other creators and players. This helps her judge which burdens are worth reducing and how far a feature should go. Players then decide whether to use these features according to their own way of playing.
Menu compatibility

Right-Click Rescue supports B42.21 single-player and multiplayer games and provides a separate Teleport Here option in the world-map context menu. When adding this option, the mod preserves existing map actions, including navigation/GPS, routes, destinations and markers. Whether menu items added by other mods work alongside it also needs to be checked for each combination.

Alongside the context menu, the mod provides an alternative keyboard shortcut that players must bind themselves. Under Options → Key Bindings → Universal Map Teleport, players can assign a key to UMTSP: Teleport Here (World Map). They can then open the world map, point to a destination and press that key to teleport their character.

caption: Figure 4  Teleport, destination and marker options displayed in the same map interface.

text: The developer first studied how different mods add menu options, then checked whether those options could work together. Checks included whether each mod's options remained visible when Map Teleport and AutoDrive loaded in different orders, whether repeatedly opening the world-map context menu produced duplicate items, and whether selecting teleport, destination and other menu items invoked their respective functions. The archived test record covers AutoDrive in two load orders, checks for duplicate menu items, and checks that selecting each item invokes its intended action. These historical records include Lua simulation checks and are not a substitute for full in-game testing across different mod combinations. [Historical test record](https://github.com/zbjgrhr/Universal-Map-Teleport-SP/blob/7727fc80130e16010101bbecda0c195815f566d6/current/mod/TEST_REPORT.md)

These checks can guide her troubleshooting if menu problems arise again. Maintenance needs to establish not only whether the teleport option appears, but also whether the other options remain present, whether any are duplicated, and whether selecting them performs the intended action.
Teleportation rules

Once character teleportation worked, the next question was whether vehicles, trailers and animals could leave with the character. A player may have spent a long time finding a suitable vehicle. Moving only the character means returning to retrieve that vehicle and its trailer. Rope-led animals may also become separated from the player after departure. She therefore added support for animals accompanying character transfers and went on to develop an edition that teleports vehicles and trailers.
What travels

The character edition provides Teleport Here. The vehicle edition retains this action and adds Teleport Vehicle Here. When Teleport Here is used from inside a vehicle, the character leaves the vehicle and teleports, while the vehicle and other passengers stay behind. Teleport Vehicle Here moves the character, other passengers and the connected convoy together. It must be initiated from inside a vehicle after the convoy has stopped; in multiplayer, the driver initiates it.

text: Based on the archived [character-edition instructions](https://github.com/zbjgrhr/Universal-Map-Teleport-SP/blob/7727fc80130e16010101bbecda0c195815f566d6/current/mod/README.md) and [vehicle-edition instructions](https://github.com/zbjgrhr/Map-Teleport---Vehicle-Trailer-Add-on/blob/db1f22e8394b073a304dd7f09b0f6cdd4ca9d3ab/current/mod/README.md). A convoy consists of the current vehicle and its connected towing chain.

The main distinction between the two actions is whether the vehicle and other passengers travel with the character. Character teleportation is available when the convoy does not need to move; vehicle teleportation is used when it does. Listing the actions separately lets players decide whether to take the convoy before they proceed.

caption: Figure 5  Vehicle-edition feature illustration showing the character and convoy teleport actions.

text: Arrival state

After a convoy transfer, the character and passengers appear outside the vehicles, with the vehicles and trailers on nearby open ground. Players can check their positions before continuing. Animals that were being led by a rope remain led by the character on arrival. The map temporarily marks the vehicle's parking position, without leaving an increasing number of markers after repeated transfers.
Usage conditions

The character edition and current vehicle edition can both be installed independently. The vehicle edition requires neither the character edition nor ZombieBuddy or another prerequisite mod. Multiplayer servers and clients must have matching versions of the mod installed.

Single-player uses direct teleportation. Multiplayer first attempts to complete the transfer in one move; if the network or map conditions at that time do not allow this, it moves in several segments instead. Pressing Esc during a segmented transfer stops the remaining journey, but does not undo movement that has already occurred or return the character to the starting point. Multiplayer functionality has undergone only initial testing and still needs checks across different servers and network environments.

The vehicle edition supports vanilla vehicles and modded vehicles that use the game's native vehicle, towing and in-vehicle animal mechanisms. Compatibility with vehicles using other custom mechanisms cannot be guaranteed on this basis.
Visual identity
The developer designed a separate visual identity for each edition, aiming to make the mod's purpose and operation apparent at a glance as players browse the Workshop.

caption: Figure 6  Character-edition identity featuring a location pin, mouse and map context menu.

text: The character edition uses a yellow location pin to represent the destination. A mouse and the Teleport Here menu item show the action: right-click the desired location on the map, then select teleport. Add Destination also appears in the image, expressing the intention that teleportation should coexist with other map actions. The name Right-Click Rescue likewise reflects the original purpose: giving players facing the same inconvenience a separate option for world-map right-click teleportation.

caption: Figure 7  Vehicle-edition identity featuring a car, an animal trailer and the Teleport Vehicle Here menu item.

text: The vehicle edition retains the yellow location pin, map grid and menu styling to give both editions a consistent series identity. The car and animals in the trailer illustrate what can travel, while the Teleport Vehicle Here menu item shows how to initiate a vehicle transfer. B42.21 and SINGLE + MULTIPLAYER identify the supported game version and single-player and multiplayer modes.

The two designs use a similar visual style to identify them as one series, while different graphics and menu wording distinguish the editions. These elements communicate what the mods do, with the aim of making their purpose clear rather than leaving players with decoration alone.

text: ZKevin's comment, translated as “It works, it saved my life,” was encouraging for the developer. Its significance to her was straightforward: a tool she had made to address her own difficulties had helped another player too. That recognition made her willing to keep investing time in improving and maintaining the mods.
Version maintenance

The mods also encountered problems early after release. The developer revised and tested them repeatedly in response to player feedback. The Workshop page retains 9 change notes for the vehicle edition, documenting the adjustments made during this period.

text: Investigating such reports begins with confirming the installed mod version and the circumstances in which the action was attempted. The instructions list several conditions to check: the vehicle edition can be installed independently, the game needs to be restarted after an update, and vehicle teleportation must be initiated from inside a vehicle. However, the available records do not establish the specific cause of JordyMaate's problem or the outcome of any retest. Removing the vehicle edition’s dependencies means players no longer need to install prerequisite mods or check their installation when troubleshooting.

She also created Bug Reports & Suggestions threads for all her mods. Players reporting a problem can provide the game version, single-player or multiplayer mode, the steps they took, the mod version and other enabled mods, and attach screenshots, error messages or the console.txt log where possible.

caption: Figure 11  Bug Reports & Suggestions thread listing the information needed for troubleshooting and the log-file location.

text: The threads give players a central place to report problems. She next plans to record the corresponding revision, test results and player retests for each issue, so that players can see its progress and earlier problems can be revisited during later maintenance.
Next steps

At this stage, the developer plans to check existing functions in different playing environments before deciding, based on feedback, whether to add new features. The priorities are whether menu items invoke their intended actions, whether characters and convoys arrive according to the transfer rules, and how each reported issue is followed up.

text: She plans to prioritize whether players can find and use the appropriate teleport menu items. She had previously been unable to find character teleportation in other mods, and after the vehicle edition was released, a player reported being unable to find its vehicle option. Both experiences show the need to keep checking menu usability. Another priority is to check the outcome of each transfer: whether all intended characters, vehicles, passengers and animals have arrived, and whether animal leads have been restored. After reloading the save, their positions and the relevant towing and leading connections also need to be checked against the expected transfer result. These situations need continued testing as versions change. Each revision should also document the issue addressed and its test results, making later checks easier and helping prevent previously reported problems from being overlooked.
Project reflection

Map Teleport began with a recurring, concrete inconvenience: when the developer wanted to teleport her character by right-clicking a location on the map, there was no usable teleport option in the menu. She made an installable tool to address this problem, then gradually added support for accompanying animals and vehicle convoys. Her concern extended beyond whether the character could reach a destination to the extra tasks a player would have to perform. She adjusted the features and instructions accordingly, aiming to reduce the additional work required before and after a transfer.

Subscriptions and comments encouraged the developer, while reports of faults also made clear the need to keep following up on players' difficulties after release. She next hopes to improve the existing functions and explain their transfer scope and usage conditions clearly, so players know how to use them and can find a feedback channel and receive a response when something goes wrong.
